newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo Q1 EPS beats estimates.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo Q1 EPS beats estimates.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said Tuesday that its first-quarter earnings per share, which exceeded analysts' estimates, were helped by double-digit domestic volume growth for its Mountain Dew brand.
The company reported net income per share of $0.27, which beat analysts' estimates by $0.03.

PepsiCo's overall sales grew 2 percent to $6.7 billion and North American beverage sales were up 4 percent, including what the company described as "solid growth" for the flagship Pepsi brand. But domestic beverage operating margins basically were unchanged from the same period a year ago, and international sales volume for beverages was down 3 percent.

PepsiCo attributed most of the domestic beverage growth to lower pricing due to lower packaging costs being passed along to the consumer, which boosted sales volume. The international decline was blamed on lower bottler case sales, lower concentrate shipments and unfavorage foreign exchange rates.
Roger Enrico, PepsiCo's chairman and chief executive, said the company is on track with its strategy of divesting its restaurants to focus on beverages and snack foods.
"We refranchised 94 stores this quarter and for the full year expect to sell as many or more than we did last year," Enrico said in a statement.
PepsiCo's Frito-Lay unit had 7 percent sales growth in North American and 13 percent growth internationally, while worldwide restaurant profits rose 7 percent.

Frito-Lay had 15 percent profit growth in North America. Internationally its operating profit was up 36 percent, helped by a gain from the sale of PepsiCo's interest in the Gerber business in Mexico. But there was a slight margin contraction, due primarily to higher wheat costs, PepsiCo said.
Bottler case sales for beverages in North America were up 6 percent, driven by strong Mountain Dew performance.
